title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a handwritten sheet of research jottings, written over a faintly visible Bourbaki typescript (draft n°370, Intégration ch. VII on Haar measure, whose neighbouring pages are pp. 225 and 227). It belongs to the 1965 'théorie de Galois des motifs' circle of ideas. Only about half the words are securely legible.

A marginal heading reads 'lien avec la conjecture de Hodge'.

The text asks the following, as far as it can be read.
(1) 'D'autre part, quels sont les foncteurs multiplicatifs de Motifs, à valeurs dans les structures de Hodge (i.e. pour les motifs sur C), qui sont [fidèles / pleinement fidèles?] ...?' In modern terms: classify the tensor (fibre) functors from the category of motives over C to the category of rational Hodge structures. Which of them are fully faithful? Full faithfulness of the Hodge realization is exactly the Hodge conjecture for products, hence the marginal link.
(2) 'Plus généralement, dans quelle mesure un morphisme de préschémas X → Y est-il [connu] par les foncteurs sur la catégorie des motifs (sur X?), et dans quelle mesure un foncteur multiplicatif peut-il être pris arbitraire !!?' This is a reconstruction question. To what extent is a scheme, or a morphism of schemes, recovered from tensor functors between categories of motives (e.g. pull-back M(Y) → M(X), or fibre functors at points)? And conversely, is every tensor functor between motive categories induced geometrically? It is a 'motivic anabelian / Tannakian reconstruction' question.
(3) 'C'est lié au pb de construction des schémas de modules pour les motifs polarisés.' Given a scheme Y (or a motive), a family of polarized motives over Y should give a map Y → Modules. Some monomorphism / representability property is mentioned. The last line, 'Y → le spectre d'un corps ......', presumably considers the case of a point, i.e. motives over a field and fields of definition / fields of moduli.

So the page links three things:
- tensor functors on motives;
- Hodge realization (the Hodge conjecture as full faithfulness);
- the existence of moduli schemes of polarized motives, whose Hodge-theoretic shadow is a period map to period domains.
errors: No mathematical claims are asserted; only questions are posed. Note that later knowledge shows tensor functors between motive categories are far from all geometric: the motivic Galois group has many automorphisms, e.g. Galois conjugation of fibre functors. So the 'arbitraire !!?' question has a largely negative answer in the naive form.

ideas.what: Hodge conjecture formulated as full faithfulness of the Hodge realization tensor functor on motives over C
ideas.modern_name: Full faithfulness of the Hodge realization; Mumford–Tate group = motivic Galois group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (standard conjectures circle, 1960s); Deligne, Milne, Serre (Motives volume 1994)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969) and the Grothendieck–Serre correspondence; explicit later in Deligne–Milne / Serre

ideas.what: Classification of tensor (fibre) functors from motives to Hodge structures or other realization categories
ideas.modern_name: Fibre functors / Tannakian torsors; comparison of realizations
ideas.where_published: Saavedra, Catégories tannakiennes; Deligne–Milne, Tannakian categories

ideas.what: To what extent morphisms of schemes are determined by (and all tensor functors arise from) functors on categories of motives
ideas.usually_credited_to: Scattered later work (e.g. reconstruction from motives or derived categories, Bondal–Orlov-type results); no single canonical credit

ideas.what: Moduli schemes of polarized motives, with the Hodge realization giving the period map
ideas.modern_name: Moduli of motives; Shimura varieties as moduli of motives; period maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Travaux de Shimura 1971; Variétés de Shimura 1979), Milne
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Récoltes et Semailles' description of 'motifs' and variation of motives; unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly ties the Hodge conjecture (full faithfulness of tensor functors to Hodge structures) to a reconstruction problem: are morphisms of schemes determined by tensor functors on motives? He also ties it to the construction of moduli schemes of polarized motives. This is an early (c. 1965) programmatic link between realization functors, motivic reconstruction and moduli of motives.
missed.quote: dans quelle mesure un foncteur multiplicatif peut-il être pris arbitraire !!? C'est lié au pb de construction des schémas de modules pour les motifs polarisés
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Moduli of motives was later realized partially, via Shimura varieties (Deligne) and Hodge loci. This page documents Grothendieck anticipating a motivic moduli theory linked with Hodge realization, earlier than usually credited. The reconstruction question remains largely unformulated in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The Hodge-conjecture-as-full-faithfulness link is standard. The explicit 1965-era pairing with moduli schemes of polarized motives and a reconstruction question is a mildly notable historical detail, but the text is fragmentary and only questions are posed.
